spine: Every week you water your fern.
You never see where the water goes.
Until the pot is cut in half.
Because of that, you see the top soil soak it up and the roots drink.
Because of that, you see the extra sink through the gravel and drain into the saucer.
Until finally you know why feed goes in the water, at the dose per litre.

acts.name: The question
acts.beats: If you water a fern, where does it all go?

acts.name: Soil
acts.beats: The top soil soaks it up first.

acts.name: Roots
acts.beats: But only the roots can drink it.

acts.name: Drainage
acts.beats: So the extra sinks through the gravel and drains into the saucer; feed in the water rides along.

acts.name: Tag
acts.beats: End card: Sprigly, one capful per litre.

output.turn: The cutaway shows the feed can only reach the roots in the water, which is why Sprigly is dosed per litre.
output.reason: An If/But/So chain with a new stop every 3-4 s; every step is plain horticulture (water soaks the top layer, roots take it up, excess drains through the gravel layer and the drainage hole).
